newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore asks Malaysia to clarify travel hitches.
newsitem.headline: Singapore asks Malaysia to clarify travel hitches.

text.p: Singapore has asked Malaysia to clarify reports some Singaporeans were having problems with Malaysian immigration procedures.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement on Friday it "has sought urgent clarification" from Malaysia's embassy "on reports that Singaporeans in Johor have not been allowed by Malaysian Immigration to leave for Singapore".

A short causeway connects Singapore to the Malaysian state of Johor. Singapore's daily Straits Times newspaper said on Friday that a number of Singaporeans who live in Johor or travel there often had been delayed by Malaysian immigration officials before being allowed to cross into Singapore.

They were asked to pay 60 ringgit ($24) for a social visit pass allowing them to remain in Malaysia for a week, and went through a complex process that included being asked why they visited Malaysia frequently, the paper said.
It said some were not able to get their passes processed by the end of the day and had to remain in Johor overnight.
Thirty people interviewed by the paper said it was the first time they had experienced such a problem.
The Straits Times quoted a Johor Baru Immigration Department spokesman as saying the operation was targeted at Singaporeans and other foreigners suspected of working in Malaysia illegally.
Last week, Malaysia Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayub said Singaporeans comprised the largest number of professional and skilled workers who worked illegally in Malaysia last year.
His comments followed a spate of sniping between Malaysia and Singapore government officials and newspapers.

Relations were strained when Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew said in a court affidavit made public early this year that Johor was "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings", sparking a heated response from Malaysia.
Lee subsequently apologised and withdrew the remarks.
